patch_description: Instead of a single hand-fixed hexagonal lattice followed by coordinate shifts, this approach is a population/relaxation hybrid: (1) generate many diverse structured seeds (different staggered-row counts, grids, corner-biased layouts, jittered hex lattices), (2) for each seed run a force-based relaxation — circles are given radii by the Gauss–Seidel solver, then centers are pushed apart along contact normals to release pressure on constrained circles (a physical "inflate-and-relax" scheme, fundamentally different from blind coordinate hill climbing since moves are driven by actual contact geometry), (3) the best seed after relaxation gets a final annealed coordinate descent with warm-started radius solves. This explores the configuration space much more broadly and lets contact-driven forces find anisotropic openings that single-axis shifts miss, while remaining deterministic (fixed RNG seeds) and fast.
